author: casparschwa
content:
I had to leave at some point but some thoughts after today's pq gasper breakout, after catching up with <@520034910149410861>: 

It seems that the biggest open question for pq gasper right now is networking: the current design has ~64 proofs floating around at >6MB. 

If pq gasper ends up needing longer slots to work, that changes the calculus quite a bit. A big part of the case for doing pq gasper ahead of pq dc is that it's a much smaller change. 

dc has networking work to do as well ofc, the signatures have to go somewhere, but it does look quite different there. But it should also be prioritized so we have a better understanding of the tradeoff here between gasper and dc. 

From what I gather this is already on people's minds as priority but just to be explicit about it and make sure we're all aligned: I'd suggest to make networking the p0 for next weeks/breakouts since it appears to be the critical decision point on weighing up pq gasper vs. dc. More Concretely: vibe-coded prototypes against current spec (which seem ~good enough for this?) and a large devnet with globally distributed nodes, so we can make the decision on more or less real numbers rather than optimistic assumptions. 

Would be great to hear from client teams if this sounds right 🙂

author: terencechain
content:
here's an attempt of DC on top of PQ: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/compare/pq...pq-dc
a few open questions:
- head vote proofs / aggregation. If head vote aggregation takes time, view merge becomes pointless. Combine head vote proof with finality vote proof into one STARK proof?
- FG vote aggregation scheme. Round vs epoch, target vs timeout, what's supported / not supported?
- FG attestation uses 1 leaf per round. Voting target -> timeout in the same round reuses the leaf and exposes the key.  Fix attestation field to use slot/epoch?
- builder payments across slots via old head votes. This can get very expensive. Can we get rid of it and lose trustless payment protection?
